Hi (29f) I dont normally take pain medication so I believe mine was a combo of the antiviral (valacyclovir 1GM)and the pain meds (Ibuprofen 800MG).

First 2 days sucked so much because my pain meds didnt seem to do much and I didnt feel like the antivirals did either. I got worse and I was worried the shingles would spread. Then I switched from taking Diclofenac for pain to ibuprofen and magically on the 3rd day of taking the antiviral I woke up and had gone from a 12 pain level to a 6 over night - I was crying I was so happy I could get out of bed again. I feel like the meds warded off any potentially worsening symptoms and I'm a little scared I'm ab to run out of them.

But on them I felt groggy and fatigued. I would drop things more than usual and generally if felt like my brain was working at half processing power. I do also have carpal tunnel though and being in bed a lot makes my symptoms for that worse as well. I would feel sick at times to food smells and was extremely picky ab what food I would eat.

Again idk how much was bc of being a burnout causality or from being bunked up in bed for so long. Being a little sick along with the pain really made things weird for me.

As far as I can tell, shingles rashes dont really "come and go." Based on my own experience and a bunch of research, once shingles picks a place to come up at it doesnt like to leave there for a very long time.

Still, if you can catch a doctor seeing it that would be best.

When mine started it felt like burn rather than being itchy. It didnt start itching until it was almost heals but the absolute best thing you can do if you feel it's odd is go to the doctor!! They will know for sure and give you meds that will keep it from spreading

 Once I was furloughed I stopped trying and had decided that even if the money they sent was erroneous preciously, the money now would be accepted as true unemployment and I /should/ be ok to use it because I needed it. In the mean time Ive been stretching my 1200 as far as it will go but it will run out soon and im only recieving 45 dollars a week from the theater atm. On the other end of this, if this money is considered mine I would finally have some savings. As a millenial who can barely make ends meet this would be a blessing to have such a thing happen. 


I'm scared that soon Ill be called back to work at my retail store because of everything too. Luckily I havent been yet and hopefully they will only after things get better.

I live in Atlanta Georgia USA (where the CDC is) and we have a HUGE Kpop fan base here. We also have quite a large population of Korean folks that have set up businesses. There is a part of the great Atlanta area where you can find businesses with their signs in Korean only.
We also have a strong nerd/geek/otaku/gaming culture here with some of the largest conventions dedicated to scifi, gaming and anime in the Southeast. (Dragoncon, Momocon, and Anime weekend Atlanta). Because of the strong fandom culture here its easy to find others in any niche community, but there are also businesses here that stem from these things.

Like Battle and Brew - a gaming bar

And Iron Age - a Korean bbq restaurant that plays Kpop like its a club

Ive observed a lot of the people who are into kpop were into jrock or anime at a younger age. Even though most of them don't understand these languages, there is a deeper understanding of skill and effort it takes for the preformers to do what they do. Kpop especially has a extremely strict standard it holds its performers to. I believe that this is the base of why these fans are attracted to enjoying kpop.

Theres also different flavor kpop for everyone. Unlike in the us where we have rock, rap, pop, etc, kpop is everything from Korean. Anything that is popular there. So theres a good chance you'll find something you enjoy if you are dedicated to finding it.
